name: Vareth Baobab-Lime Tonic
description: A crisp, slightly bitter tonic water built around baobab fruit extract and Kaffir lime, marketed as a digestive aid and electrolyte replenishment drink. The bitterness is real and unapologetic — Vareth positioned this as an adult alternative to sweeter mainstream sodas.
flavor_profile: Earthy baobab tartness, Kaffir lime sharpness, quinine-style bitterness, clean and dry finish
cultural_context: Vareth Baobab-Lime Tonic has a devoted Tier 3 following among people who consider themselves too sophisticated for mainstream sodas but can't justify Tier 4 pricing. It's a staple at mid-range izakaya-style bars as a mixer and a standalone. The branding leans into exclusivity without being overtly luxurious.
story_hooks: Vareth's 'functional' health claims are under investigation by a Meridian 88 consumer authority — the electrolyte content may be within legal limits but the digestive aid marketing is borderline fraudulent.
A bar owner in a transitional Tier 2-3 neighborhood built her entire cocktail menu around Vareth pairings — when supply dries up without explanation, she starts investigating the distributor.
A corporate wellness program mandates Vareth Tonic as the approved beverage for augmentation recovery wards — someone inside the program is getting a kickback.
